data.draft:
The sky appears blue because of a phenomenon called Rayleigh scattering, which is the scattering of light by small particles or molecules in the atmosphere. When sunlight enters Earth's atmosphere, it encounters tiny molecules of gases such as nitrogen and oxygen, and these molecules scatter the light in all directions.
The amount of scattering that occurs depends on the wavelength of the light, with shorter wavelengths being scattered more than longer wavelengths. Since blue light has a shorter wavelength compared to other colors in the visible spectrum, such as red or orange, it is scattered more intensely by the tiny molecules in the atmosphere, giving the sky its characteristic blue appearance during the daytime, especially in the direction of the sun.
